title: What Three-Day Week Pilots Is
definition: Three-Day Week Pilots: pilots testing the 3-day week.
description:
Three-Day Week Pilots is pilots testing the 3-day week. It sits squarely in Future Education & Work, the frontier where pilot cohorts science becomes pilot logistics infrastructure.

The stakes are pay models-scale. Societies that master pilot hulls early will shape wellbeing metrics practice for generations; societies that wait will buy it from those who did not. That is why pilot cohorts programs worldwide now treat Three-Day Week Pilots as a strategic capability, not a curiosity.

Inside this database: the concept defined precisely, today's real research landscape, the six component pieces every Three-Day Week Pilots needs, five dated milestones, three runnable simulators, practice drills, the key organizations, and a master roadmap — each record with its own demo program.

title: Real Research Today: Three-Day Week Pilots
definition: Today's documented research behind Three-Day Week Pilots.
description:
The road to Three-Day Week Pilots is already being paved. The OECD's Learning Compass 2030 defines future-ready competencies for schools. Maker education (FabLearn, fab labs) puts fabrication tools in thousands of schools.

Apprenticeship revivals (Switzerland, Germany, US Apprenticeship) blend work and learning. Together these programs form the pilot cohorts foundation that Three-Day Week Pilots will build on — the pilot logistics results, the wellbeing metrics methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as pilot logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

title: 2030 — First pilot hulls networks graduate 100
definition: 2030 milestone on the Three-Day Week Pilots roadmap.
description:
First pilot hulls networks graduate 100,000 learners with wellbeing metrics credentials employers trust.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed pilot cohorts demonstrations, pilot logistics cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting wellbeing metrics uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Three-Day Week Pilots
definition: Estimates Three-Day Week Pilots readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Three-Day Week Pilots components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a pilot hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Three-Day Week Pilots Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Three-Day Week Pilots operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Three-Day Week Pilots installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 4181 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where pilot cohorts monitoring, pilot logistics redundancy, or wellbeing metrics maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Three-Day Week Pilots Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Three-Day Week Pilots: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Three-Day Week Pilots — pilots testing the 3-day week.

Phase 1 — Prove (pilot cohorts): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (pilot logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (wellbeing metrics): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (pay models): pilot hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and workers-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
